Disable CloudTrail in the training account so bucket access attempts are never recorded anywhere
explain: A gateway endpoint policy filters which buckets and actions are reachable through that endpoint. Scoping it to the data-lake ARNs blocks exfiltration to outside buckets even if IAM is broader.

q: An endpoint runs two production variants with weights 90 and 10. Where is this traffic split defined?
options: In the endpoint configuration as InitialVariantWeight per production variant
In the KMS key rotation schedule attached to the endpoint each quarter
In the CloudTrail trail selector configured for SageMaker data events
In the Model Card markdown describing the intended use of each model version for reviewers
explain: Each production variant in the endpoint configuration carries an InitialVariantWeight. The weights determine the share of InvokeEndpoint traffic each variant serves.

q: Traffic triples every evening and collapses at night. Which auto-scaling setup handles this while controlling cost?
options: A fixed fleet sized for the evening peak that keeps running around the clock every day
Manual instance changes approved by email once per quarter after capacity reviews
Target tracking on InvocationsPerInstance with a sensible minimum, maximum, and scale-in cooldown
Retrain the model hourly so smaller instances can serve larger loads, skipping validation gates to save time
explain: Target tracking adds capacity when per-instance invocations rise and removes it during quiet hours. Min and max bounds plus a scale-in cooldown prevent flapping and runaway cost.

q: A blue/green endpoint update must roll back automatically when error-rate alarms fire during the shift. How is this configured?
options: By emailing metrics to managers and waiting for their manual approval to proceed
By disabling all CloudWatch alarms for the duration of the deployment window
By routing 100 percent of traffic instantly and deleting the blue environment right after the shift
With a blue/green DeploymentConfig using CloudWatch alarms and auto-rollback on alarm
explain: SageMaker blue/green deployments accept a list of CloudWatch alarms with an auto-rollback flag. When an alarm fires during baking, traffic shifts back to blue automatically.
source: Adattata da Udemy – practice test MLA-C01

q: Security must run SQL forensics over SageMaker API activity across regions for the last year. Which approach scales best?
options: Scroll the console event history region by region for each audit week
Query CloudTrail Lake, which stores immutable event data queryable with SQL
Recompute Model Monitor baselines and compare the constraint JSON files by hand
Parse KMS rotation emails forwarded by the compliance mailbox into spreadsheets
explain: CloudTrail Lake ingests management and data events into an immutable store with a SQL interface, suited to multi-region forensic queries over long retention windows.

q: After retraining with new features, feature-attribution drift alerts fire constantly even though quality is fine. What is the likely cause?
options: The SHAP baseline still reflects the old feature set and must be regenerated from the new training data
The KMS key for captures expired, so payloads are now stored in plaintext in the bucket
The VPC security group blocks CloudWatch from reading the new endpoint metrics after the update
The endpoint IAM role lost permission to write CloudTrail digest files, breaking the audit trail for reviewers
explain: Attribution drift compares live SHAP values against the stored baseline. Retraining with different features invalidates that reference, so a fresh baseline from the new training data is required.

q: Only callers inside an approved VPC may invoke a sensitive endpoint. Which IAM enforcement fits?
options: A wildcard allow policy on sagemaker InvokeEndpoint granted to every identity in the whole account
A resource policy opening the endpoint to any AWS authenticated caller across all accounts for partner access
An identity policy condition on aws:SourceVpce or aws:SourceVpc restricting calls to the approved endpoint or VPC
A scheduled rotation of every caller password every 30 days, enforced through IAM password policies on all users with alerts
explain: Condition keys such as aws:SourceVpce and aws:SourceVpc bind InvokeEndpoint permission to requests arriving through the approved VPC endpoint or VPC, denying outside callers.

q: A deployment pipeline must block promotion of any model version lacking reviewer approval. Which registry mechanism enforces this?
options: Model Registry approval status checked as a pipeline gate before the deploy stage
A CloudWatch dashboard widget turning green when latency looks healthy after deploys
Data capture sampling raised to 100 percent during the rollout week for analysis
KMS automatic rotation enabled on the artifact bucket before every release of the pipeline
explain: Model Registry versions carry an approval status such as PendingManualApproval or Approved. The pipeline gate reads that status and halts promotion until reviewers approve.

q: The team rotates the KMS CMK yearly but retraining code must keep working without edits. What practice makes rotation seamless?
options: Hardcode the key ID string in every training script and notebook used
Disable rotation entirely so ciphertexts never change across pipeline runs each year
Reference the key by alias and let automatic rotation replace backing material
Share one data key across dev, staging, and production environments to simplify access
explain: Code referencing the alias always resolves to the current key material. With automatic rotation, AWS replaces backing keys yearly while the alias stays stable.

q: A monitoring schedule detects severe data drift at 3 AM. Which event pattern wakes the retraining workflow?
options: A monthly Cost Explorer report delivered to the finance mailbox and reviewed before any retraining decision is approved
A Model Card comment thread mentioning drift in free text, escalated to reviewers by email for triage within two business days
A VPC Flow Log entry showing a rejected connection on port 443, forwarded to the retraining queue by a filter as a proxy for drift remediation
An EventBridge rule matching the SageMaker monitor job state-change event with a violation status that starts a Step Functions workflow
explain: Model Monitor emits job state-change events to EventBridge. A rule filtering on the violation status routes them to the retraining workflow, such as Step Functions or a Pipelines execution.
